text:
Every company using AI should be asking one question: what happens if your provider says no?

That might mean a refused request, a changed policy, or an outage at the worst possible moment.

Mistral's new release, **Mistral Large 4**, is a strong argument for keeping your most critical AI workloads under your own control.

**Why business leaders should pay attention:**

**🏢 It's built for real work, not just chat.**
It scores 59.9% on AutomationBench and 1,393 Elo on AA-Briefcase, two benchmarks that measure business workflows and long, multi-step professional tasks. Its coding-agent results put it ahead of DeepSeek V4 Pro and Qwen3.8 Max.

**🛡️ It handles sensitive security work.**
Your security team can use it to reproduce and patch vulnerabilities (82%, the top reported score), analyse malware, and write detection rules. These are tasks that some closed models simply refuse.

**🔑 You control where it runs.**
Because the weights are open, you can run it in your own cloud, on-prem, or on Dell AI servers with ready-made deployment recipes. Your code, logs and data stay with you.

**📄 Check the licence.**
It ships under the Mistral Ecosystem Open-Weight License, which is based on MIT but restricts model-as-a-service offerings. Internal use is straightforward. If you plan to resell it as a hosted API, have legal review the terms first.

**The bigger picture:**
Not long ago, "open" meant "a generation behind." This model ranks #5 among open-weight models on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index and posts frontier-level results in coding and cybersecurity.

The choice between capability and control is narrowing quickly.

Is your organisation planning for a mix of open and closed models, or still all-in on one provider? 👇
